Title: Verify a test shop with representative sample data exists
Preconditions: Access to the QA environment with the feature enabled.
Test Data: Target test shop identifier (from PM/QA lead).
Steps:
1. Log in as an Administrator and open the target test shop.
2. Navigate to Work Orders.
3. Navigate to Customers.
4. Navigate to the Parts department (Part Sales, Catalog & Inventory, Vendor & Order Management).
5. Navigate to Invoicing.
6. Navigate to Schedule.
Expected Results:
1. Shop loads without error.
2. At least a few sample work orders exist, including at least one with work-order lines.
3. At least a few sample customers exist.
4. Sample parts, at least one catalog/inventory record, and at least one vendor with an order exist.
5. At least one sample invoice exists.
6. At least one sample appointment exists.
Expected Final Result: The test shop contains observable sample data across work orders, WO lines, customers, parts, vendors, invoices, and schedule appointments, so permission effects (hidden/disabled/blocked actions) are observable during testing. If any area is empty, seed it or request seeding before proceeding.

Title: Verify an Administrator test account can reach role and staff administration
Preconditions: CR-SETUP-001 passed. Administrator credentials available.
Test Data: Administrator account email/password.
Steps:
1. Log in as the Administrator test account.
2. Open Administration > Roles and Permissions.
3. Open Administration > Staff.
Expected Results:
1. Login succeeds.
2. The Roles and Permissions list page loads and is accessible to this account.
3. The Staff page loads and is accessible to this account.
Expected Final Result: The Administrator test account can reach both Administration > Roles and Permissions and Administration > Staff. This account is the driver for all role configuration and staff-assignment test cases.

Title: Provision one dedicated test user per system role
Preconditions: CR-SETUP-002 passed. CR-SETUP-004 confirms the templates are seeded.
Test Data: Naming convention for test users, e.g. `qa-<role>@shopview-test.com` (one per role).
Steps:
1. As Administrator, open Administration > Staff.
2. For each of the 12 system roles, create (or confirm there exists) a dedicated test user whose role is set to that system role: Administrator, Service Manager, Senior Service Advisor, Service Advisor, Foreman, Technician, Parts Manager, Parts Technician, Office, Sales Representative, Time Clock. (Note: the matrix names 11 roles; see the Owner discrepancy in the README.)
3. Record each test user's credentials in the shared QA credential store.
Expected Results:
1. Staff list loads.
2. A distinct, loginable test user exists for each system role.
3. Credentials are recorded and retrievable.
Expected Final Result: There is exactly one dedicated, loginable test user per system role. These users let each role's permissions be verified by logging in as that user. If creation is not possible in this environment, note which users must be provisioned by an admin before role-specific files can run.

Title: Verify the 12 system role templates are seeded and visible
Preconditions: CR-SETUP-002 passed.
Test Data: Expected role names (see spec / file 12).
Steps:
1. As Administrator, open Administration > Roles and Permissions.
2. Review the list of roles marked as system/template roles.
3. Confirm the following are listed: Administrator, Service Manager, Senior Service Advisor, Service Advisor, Foreman, Technician, Parts Manager, Parts Technician, Office, Sales Representative, Time Clock.
4. Count the system roles.
Expected Results:
1. The roles list page loads.
2. The system role templates are present and labeled as system roles.
3. All listed roles are present.
4. Count matches the PM-confirmed number. Spec says 12 but the matrix names 11 (Owner merged into Admin) — flag any mismatch per the README discrepancy list.
Expected Final Result: All expected system role templates are seeded and visible on the Roles and Permissions list page. Any deviation in the set or count is logged against the README discrepancy note (item 1).

Title: Verify "role change forces logout" behavior and set up efficient two-session testing
Preconditions: CR-SETUP-003 provided at least one non-admin test user. Two browsers or one browser + incognito available.
Test Data: One non-admin test user (e.g. the Technician test user) and the Administrator account.
Steps:
1. In Browser A, log in as the non-admin test user and remain on any page.
2. In Browser B (or incognito), log in as Administrator, open Administration > Staff, and change the test user's role to a different role. Save.
3. In Browser A, perform an action or navigate.
4. In Browser A, log the test user back in.
Expected Results:
1. User is logged in.
2. Role change saves successfully.
3. The test user is logged out (session invalidated) as a result of the role change.
4. The newly assigned role's permissions are now in effect.
Expected Final Result: Changing a user's role forces that user to log out; the new role applies on next login. QA must expect this between test runs. Use two browsers/incognito (admin in one, test user in the other) to reconfigure roles and re-log-in efficiently.

Title: Establish reset guidance between test cases
Preconditions: CR-SETUP-003 and CR-SETUP-004 passed.
Test Data: None.
Steps:
1. Before a case that modifies a system role's permissions, note the role's current settings (or plan to Reset to Template if that feature is confirmed available — see README item 6).
2. After a case that modified a role or created a custom role, restore the modified system role to its documented defaults and delete any custom roles created solely for the test.
3. After a case that reassigned a test user's role, reassign that user back to its dedicated system role and re-log-in per CR-SETUP-005.
Expected Results:
1. Baseline captured.
2. Environment returns to a known clean baseline.
3. Test users are back on their dedicated roles.
Expected Final Result: Between test cases, roles, custom roles, and test-user assignments are reset to the known baseline so cases do not interfere with each other. Prefer editing/deleting via the admin UI; use Reset to Template only once its behavior is PM-confirmed.

2. Columns are present in order: Role Name, Type, Template, Description, Users Assigned, Actions.
3. Type shows "System"; Template shows "—"; Users Assigned shows a numeric count; Description is shown.

5. A "Create Custom Role" button is visible and enabled.
Expected Final Result: The list page displays every role with all six columns correctly populated, distinguishing System vs Custom rows, and exposes the Create Custom Role button.

Title: View Permissions opens read-only summary from the list page

1. Click "Create Custom Role".
2. Select one of the 12 system templates ("Technician") and continue.

4. Review the Permission Editor (CRUD grid, WO sub-settings, Parts Department, Invoicing, Timesheets, Page Access toggles, Settings, View Mode, Cross-Cutting toggles) and adjust one permission.
5. Click Save.
6. Locate the new role in the list.
Expected Results:
1. The create flow opens on the Template Selection step.
2. Template is selected; flow advances to Role Details with settings pre-filled from the template.
3. Flow advances to the Permission Editor.
4. The editor shows all sections; the adjusted permission updates.
5. Validation passes; the role is saved and the user returns to the list page.
6. "Senior Tech QA" appears with Type = Custom and Template = Technician.
Expected Final Result: A new custom role is created via the four-step flow and appears in the list with the correct Type and source Template.

Title: Template selection pre-fills all settings
Preconditions: Logged in as Administrator; Create Custom Role flow open.
Test Data: Template with a known permission profile (e.g., "Parts Manager").
Steps:
1. On Template Selection, choose a template with a distinctive profile ("Parts Manager").
2. Advance to the Permission Editor.
3. Complete Name and save; then open View Permissions for the new role.
Expected Results:
1. Template is highlighted/selected; 12 templates are available to choose from.
2. All permissions (CRUD grid, toggles, view mode, etc.) are pre-populated to match the chosen template's defaults, not blank.
3. The saved role retains the template reference and the pre-filled values as adjusted.
Expected Final Result: Choosing a template pre-fills every setting from that template and records it as the role's source template.

Title: Create Custom Role blocked on duplicate name
Preconditions: Logged in as Administrator; an existing role named "Senior Tech QA" exists (e.g., from CR-ROLEMGMT-005).

Expected Final Result: Duplicate role names are rejected with a uniqueness validation error; a unique name succeeds.

Title: CRUD cascade enabling (View ← Edit ← Delete)
Preconditions: Logged in as Administrator; Permission Editor open (create or edit); a permission area with all CRUD off.
Test Data: Any CRUD area (e.g., Work Orders) starting with View/Edit/Delete all OFF.
Steps:
1. In an area with all CRUD OFF, enable **Edit**.
2. Reset the area to all OFF, then enable **Delete**.
3. Confirm the auto-enabled checkboxes reflect in the grid immediately.
Expected Results:
1. Edit turns ON and View auto-enables.
2. Delete turns ON and both Edit and View auto-enable.
3. The dependent checkboxes visibly become checked without a page reload.
Expected Final Result: Enabling Edit cascades to View; enabling Delete cascades to Edit and View.

Title: CRUD cascade disabling (Delete → Edit → View)
Preconditions: Logged in as Administrator; Permission Editor open; a CRUD area with View/Edit/Delete all ON.
Test Data: Any CRUD area (e.g., Work Orders) starting with all CRUD ON.
Steps:
1. In an area with all CRUD ON, disable **Edit**.
2. Reset to all ON, then disable **View**.
3. Confirm the state after each action.
Expected Results:
1. Edit turns OFF and Delete auto-disables; View remains ON.
2. View turns OFF and both Edit and Delete auto-disable.
3. Downstream checkboxes update immediately and consistently.
Expected Final Result: Disabling View disables Edit and Delete; disabling Edit disables Delete — cascade works in the downward direction.

Title: Delete a custom role with 0 users assigned
Preconditions: Logged in as Administrator; a custom role with 0 users assigned exists.

Steps:

2. Click Delete in the Actions column.
3. Confirm the deletion.
4. Refresh/re-check the list.
Expected Results:

2. A confirmation dialog appears.
3. The role is deleted and disappears from the list.
4. The role is no longer present.
Expected Final Result: A custom role with no assigned users is deleted after confirmation and removed from the list.

Title: Delete blocked for a custom role with users assigned
Preconditions: Logged in as Administrator; a custom role with 1+ users assigned exists.
Test Data: Custom role with Users Assigned = N (N ≥ 1).
Steps:
1. Confirm the target custom role shows Users Assigned ≥ 1.
2. Click Delete in the Actions column.
3. Observe the Delete button state in the modal.
4. Reassign all users off the role (via Staff page), then retry Delete.

4. Once Users Assigned = 0, Delete proceeds via the standard confirmation and succeeds.
Expected Final Result: Deletion is blocked with the "Cannot Delete" modal while users are assigned; after reassignment the role becomes deletable.
